new feedback

_Hi! Yesterday I vibe-coded a new app and decided to try Adapty for subscriptions :)_
_Shame there’s no MCP for the initial setup, so Claude could create the products and hook up the stores itself, but everything else was super easy_ :fire:
Another +1 point for us to release MCP
MCPs are dead, CLI is a way to go. and we have <https://adapty.io/docs/developer-cli-reference|one>
This does not resonate with our customers and prospects, we keep receiving MCP requests
That's just until some influencer drops a truth bomb on them about the death of MCP
But we do advise them to use CLI and our skill for agents when they ask for MCP, right?

Yes, but:
1. Our CLI is still limited
2. People want MCP explicitly

Our (hypothetical) MCP will have exactly the same limitations as CLI. And they don't want MCP, they want a way to pair their agents with our backend, which is associated with the word "MCP". The only use-case when MCP is strictly unavoidable is when someone wants to use it from web version of Claude, but this is not related to dev process
Also, I'm not so sure that it is so strict now, actually web Claude can run stuff in a sandbox, so maybe it can even run CLI, didn't try it for quiet a while
<@U08QUJMN0UV> fyi, please share a bit on how our CLI rules the world
it seems like without MCP we index worse in Claude
That sucks. Than we have to roll out our MCP before they roll out their next model
Coming soon: `adapty integrate` and `adapty migrate` commands for CLI. You run just one command, and your agent creates products and other entities and integrates the Adapty SDK in 10 minutes
Just to be clear, having MCP != being advised by Claude. It might just suggest the bigger competitor as a default choice
<@U07J9LKBQ5U> hi! is it under your Core team umbrella?

<@U07MXM412JV> I believe the correct way to put it is that it’s currently under no one’s umbrella. From the backend (Core) side, we can extend the CLI’s capabilities by adding new endpoints for it to call. However, it’s harder to say who owns MCP.

<@U9HDNS9S4>, maybe you can share a few words here? As we discussed, our AI team is currently focused on the AI part of the Flow Builder. Once that’s finished, they’ll get back to working on MCP and the rest of the AI-related initiatives.
that's correct, they are currently on AI builder initiatives, they will take CLI/MCP and agentic experience in general in October
Thank you for clarifying

entries.message:
Feature: <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/ADP-6445|Apple Retention Messaging API>
Release: July 30, 2026 (under feature flag)
Dependencies: None
Effected areas: Dashboard (new section), Analytics

<!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <!subteam^S03KC9S1QMC> <@U05QELDHUUX> <@U06K36L6CTB>

Sup, team — it’s finally here (under feature flag BUT goes live this week)! :apple:

When a subscriber taps Cancel Subscription in iOS Settings, Apple now shows _your_ message right in the cancellation sheet — a value reminder, a discount, or a plan switch — before the cancellation is confirmed. The one screen apps never owned, now addressable straight from Adapty:

• on-device preview — see the message in Apple’s cancel sheet (light & dark) before it goes to review (Our benefit, only SW support)
• AI localization — write once in English, auto translate fills every locale. (Our benefit, RC and SW doesn’t support this)
• save-rate analytics — Shown / Saved / Save rate per message
Apple’s side is still in beta, so we’re shipping behind a feature flag purely as a safety net. Until it comes off, enable it in the browser console:
`window.adapty_ff.set('retentionMessaging', true)` → Apple Retention Messaging appears in the left nav. Poke around and drop anything odd in this thread. <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> You can provide it to your clients who are approved from Apple, most probably we’ll disable it this week and go LIVE!

*Who this is for:* 
Any iOS subscription app that wants to lift retention with zero engineering - no endpoint, no SDK update. Sharpest fits: price-sensitive apps (discount at cancel intent), monthly + annual mixes (plan switch instead of churn).

*What’s next:* 
Analytics improvements (adding saved $ metric), then A/B testing if adoption is strong.

Docs: <https://adapty.io/docs/retention-messaging|adapty.io/docs/retention-messaging>

Huge kudos to <@U0ACSQAKJA1> <@U09AH7D2A4X> <@U0AQZG23D62> <@U0A3M160RB4> <@U08ASB4GYR4> <@U0AKC1Y09R8> :fire:

entries.name: *AI Agent (Apple Ads) - what two months of client conversations tell us*
entries.message:
*AI Agent (Apple Ads) - what two months of client conversations tell us*

I've analyzed every client conversation with the agent since release. In this post, I'll share the main highlights. You can find the full analysis in the document: <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-18-27-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|:bar_chart: AI Agent Chat Analytics> + interactive visualization attached.

*The numbers*:
• 81 client orgs tried the agent → 221 real chats
• *72% of orgs (58) started one chat and never came back* :epic-sad:
• 11 deep sessions with 10+ messages - clients execute its instructions step by step and come back for verification.
*What separates those who stayed from those who left:*
• Churned clients opened with broad questions - "what's wrong with my ads?" in various forms. The agent answered, couldn't create or change anything itself, and the client never returned.
• Retained clients came with specific tasks - "what's up with my ROAS?" - which gives them a reason to come back and re-check regularly. One client literally runs the same weekly-report prompt every Monday across 3–4 apps, polishing it a bit each iteration.
*Potential agent improvements:*
1. Scheduled reports/checks - "check my ROAS every Monday."
2. Agent-initiated follow-ups - client asks "what can I improve?", agent gives recommendations and offers: "Want me to re-check in 3 days and ping you?" with an "Ok, remind me" button. Should lift retention for clients who come with broad questions.
Attached to the message is a visualization of the analytics in the form of an HTML file.
You can also find an MD file with analytics <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-Agent-Chat-Analytics-May-25-July-28-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|in the Document>.

[Roman Kuntsevich]: *AI Agent (Apple Ads) - what two months of client conversations tell us*

I've analyzed every client conversation with the agent since release. In this post, I'll share the main highlights. You can find the full analysis in the document: <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-18-27-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|:bar_chart: AI Agent Chat Analytics> + interactive visualization attached.

*The numbers*:
• 81 client orgs tried the agent → 221 real chats
• *72% of orgs (58) started one chat and never came back* :epic-sad:
• 11 deep sessions with 10+ messages - clients execute its instructions step by step and come back for verification.
*What separates those who stayed from those who left:*
• Churned clients opened with broad questions - "what's wrong with my ads?" in various forms. The agent answered, couldn't create or change anything itself, and the client never returned.
• Retained clients came with specific tasks - "what's up with my ROAS?" - which gives them a reason to come back and re-check regularly. One client literally runs the same weekly-report prompt every Monday across 3–4 apps, polishing it a bit each iteration.
*Potential agent improvements:*
1. Scheduled reports/checks - "check my ROAS every Monday."
2. Agent-initiated follow-ups - client asks "what can I improve?", agent gives recommendations and offers: "Want me to re-check in 3 days and ping you?" with an "Ok, remind me" button. Should lift retention for clients who come with broad questions.

Feature: <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/ADP-5994|Virtual currencies support>
Release date: July 21, 2026
Dependencies: None

<!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <!subteam^S03KC9S1QMC> <@U05QELDHUUX> <@U06K36L6CTB> It’s finally here! :money-smell:

You can now define in-app currencies - credits, tokens, coins - link them to your products, and Adapty will automatically grant and track balances for every user.

*Who this is for:*
• *AI apps* - charge credits per generation, bundle a monthly allowance into subscriptions, sell credit packs as one-time products
• *Short drama / video apps* - coins to unlock episodes
• *Games* - soft + hard currency with atomic conversions
• *Education & productivity* - hearts, lives, metered actions like OCR or exports
*How it works:*
Сreate a currency, map it to products with credit amounts, and every purchase or renewal credits the user automatically. Reading and spending balances happens through the *server-side API.* 

*What’s next:*
If adoption is strong, we’re planning Flow Builder support (analogue of product variables), manual credits from the dashboard, SDK methods, and balance-based segments to target paywalls.

Docs: <https://adapty.io/docs/virtual-currencies|adapty.io/docs/virtual-currencies>

Huge kudos to: <@U08ASB4GYR4> <@U09AH7D2A4X> <@U0A3M160RB4> <@U0AQZG23D62> <@U0AKC1Y09R8>

that's what I told about ledger security <@U07J9LKBQ5U>

<@U08EVBTE69E> We handle this by splitting coins by source. Coins bought as consumable IAP are always non-expiring - Apple 3.1.1 requires that, so we don’t fight it.

Coins granted by a subscription can be set as expiring: they burn at the end of each billing cycle, and when the subscription expires, whatever’s left burns too. So cancelling doesn’t let you stockpile subscription coins.

Spending is FIFO: expiring coins (closest expiry first) are always spent before non-expiring ones. So users burn through their subscription coins first, and the purchased “forever” coins are only touched last.

The “cancel and just buy coin packs” path stays open - Apple requires it.

hey team,

need some help with Readability who is evaluating RC needs some answers and ready to sign now if we can give the right AND ACCURATE responses.

i go into more detail but overall they feel like the onboarding is a incomplete product, and that RC, has a great onboarding and paywall builder in comparison to us. this goes against all internal dialogue so i hope we can turn these questions into feedback and action items.

quick background:

• legacy reading/education app
• 21k+ 5-star reviews
• ~$250k MRR today
• existing FunnelFox customer
• evaluating Adapty vs RevenueCat (RC is "more mature and has a better onboarding builder" 
• expects to scale roughly 2-2.5x before the end of 2026
they are already invested in FunnelFox and want to stay in our ecosystem if we can confidently answer a few questions. details all below:

<@U9HDNS9S4>

• does the new onboarding builder support sign in/sign up with Apple, Google, Facebook, email, and existing account login?
• can they place authentication both before and after the paywall within the onboarding flow?
• can they make API calls during onboarding and write/read data from their backend?
• will custom HTML/script support be available in the new onboarding builder and when?
• how confident are we that Android support for the onboarding builder ships in early July?
• what is the status and ETA for React Native integration with flow builder ?
<@U9HDNS9S4> / <@U0AGF7L13L5>

• RC has Amazon support and they sell on amazon, is this on our road map. when? 
• what is the status and ETA for Apple Retention Messaging?
they also have concerns stemming from their FunnelFox implementation and the Braintree workarounds they had to build.
need clarity on:


• entitlement management for Braintree subscriptions
• app access for Braintree subscribers
• analytics visibility
• can Braintree subscriptions be imported and used for entitlement/access management inside Adapty?
• how historical Braintree subscription data would be migrated
• engineering lift required
• known limitations
<@U08EVBTE69E>

RevenueCat was positioned as having a massive template library and a more mature onboarding platform.

they brought templates up multiple times throughout the call as a way to reduce implementation time and get to best practices faster.

• when can we realistically expect onboarding templates?
• when could we realistically promise onboarding templates for children's education/reading apps?
one additional note:

they only plan to run 3 onboarding/paywall flows initially.

if we can answer the questions above and get those first few flows stood up, I think we win this deal. PS is obviously slammed, but I don't think we need a huge engagement here to get them over the finish line.

<@U074DLWC5L7> <@U08MPLZ50NP> if we cannot have templates and SSO and everything else they need would it be possible to build 1-3 funnels and paywalls for them? this is a RC head to head and will be over 500MRR in less than 6 months.

appreciate any guidance.

cc: <@U034A27SVHC> if you would like to join the call i added you as optional

entries.message:
Hi there! I suppose sometimes core-related posts will look less like a cool new feature for customers. So, this is a story about an invisible defensive feature: the kind that hopefully no customer ever notices, because its whole purpose is to prevent bad things from happening in the background.
It was implemented and delivered a sprint ago, but I believe that late is better than never.

*What's the deal?* 
The main problem this feature revolves around is "Forwarding event loops".
Adapty allows its users to forward events into third-party systems for further processing and that's perfectly fine - many customers, especially big ones use it. However, the issue is that we have no control over what our customers do in other systems in terms of event routing. And rarely, but very painfully we encountered situations where some of our customers were configuring third-party systems in a way that forwarded events further... back to Adapty.
Easy to guess, what happened next: reforward back to them, receive again, repeat until (almost) forever (but most likely until something breaks under the load). So given that, if someone configured back-forwarding and experienced a spike of events (say a lot of transactions in a short period of time) - we're cooked, just like Spider-Man's "no you!" meme but on high speed. Why is it bad? Well, apart from useless load on our metal, we had already experienced a few painful downtimes of the integrations pipeline because of it.

*Aha, and what you did?*
To prevent this, we added a small layer of event analysis on the fly for the integrations flow: before forwarding, we decompose an event in a store-based manner (separately App Store v1, v2 and Play Store), combine some of its data into `deduplication key` - like a passport for an event and store it in memory for an hour at the moment of forwarding. If an App Store / Play Store related event is about to be forwarded and its deduplication key is already present, we simply do nothing integration-wise. That's it.
We shipped it in two stages: for the first week, we just added a few logs/notifications around such suspicious passengers, to see if it worked at all. Surprising discoveries around it were that even at this stage there were a few really small customers with such loops. Only around 1-2 transactions per day, but still buzzing every minute or so on constant ping-ponging events back and forth. The second stage, obviously, was about transforming alerts into strict bans on forwarding.
We haven’t had a real forward-storm since then, which is good news, but the mechanism is already catching small misconfigurations.

Big thanks go to <@U04B26DSWMA> for implementing the first version, <@U0AR243M9T9> for the initial review, and <@UNWFN144R> for the review battle that helped make this thing nice and robust.

*P.S.* We’re a bit behind with this feed, but next week we’ll catch up and share a few more recent releases - about integrations, billing, and the initial work on Virtual Currencies and Apple Retention Messaging API.

entries.name: *Problem*
entries.message:
*Problem*

The <!subteam^S0ATWJA5K6Z> has identified the root cause behind our recurring incidents related to connection pool exhaustion between Odyssey and Postgres. During purchase validation, we create a lot of records (transactions, PAL, subscriptions, non-subscriptions, transaction events, and a few others). Since this operation has to be atomic, it all happens inside a single transaction / single PG connection. As a result, Postgres accumulates a lot of uncommitted row versions that stick around for quite a while, which slows the database down once the number of concurrent operations crosses a certain threshold.

There are basically two ways to address this kind of issue:
1. Reduce the number of operations running in parallel.
2. Reduce how long each operation takes.
*Solution*

We’ve moved App Store and Play Store purchase event processing to a background job (similar to how Stripe and Paddle do it) and added rate-limiting on concurrent event handling (processing metrics are available <https://grafana.adpinfra.dev/d/dramatiq-workers/dramatiq-workers?orgId=1&var-namespace=production&var-queue=purchase_app_store&var-queue=purchase_play_store&var-actor=All&from=now-15m&to=now|here>). This smooths out event handling over time and protects us from sudden spikes coming from the stores. Nothing changes on the SDK side: we still validate purchases and grant PAL on time, no delays there.

We also did a small refactor of the core transaction validation module, which cut the time a transaction stays open by around 60%.

Technical details are in this <https://gitlab.adapty.io/adapty/adapty-dashboard-api/-/merge_requests/12810|MR>.

*Risks*

If customers start complaining about delayed event delivery to their hooks (custom webhooks or raw event forwarding), or about issues with granting PAL, ping <!subteam^S09JZKWUF2N>.

thread.text:
Feature: <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-77?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZDIwOTUyM2NkY2MzNGVhYzk3ZTc5ODQ0YzZiNmQzNWYiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|Aerospike profile migrations>
Release date: May 6th, 2026 11:43 UTC
Affected areas: Universe

We have stopped writing data to Postgres tables `adapty_analytics_profile`, `adapty_analytics_profile_installation_meta`, `adapty_analytics_profile_attribute`, `adapty_analytics_profile_attribution_unified`, `adapty_purchase_profile_purchase_state` which were previously responsible for profile state. For any research or support purposes, Aerospike is a single source of truth from now on. It can be accessed via web-interface <https://aerospike.prod.adpinfra.dev/|here>.
For info regrading access there, please refer to <https://adapty-team.slack.com/archives/C060EEW2FEV/p1774604905415179|this> message (I believe, everyone who is eligible for this access is a member of that channel already)
<!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> FYI
There will be several minor releases afterwards, mostly boring tech debt elimination. All moving parts are already in place, and, as usual, if something suspicious surfaces, please let us know
<@U04B26DSWMA> could you add me and @ Hudson Ribeiro to that secret channel too
<@U08C43RCH39> I believe, you can handle this (access to Aerospike dashboard, I mean)

Just to clarify - there will never be access to Aerospike on a mass scale as it was with Postgres. This is due to infrastructure (analytic queries may impact production), as well as privacy and security concerns. We'd like to keep number of non-dev employees with an access somewhat below 10, and leave it mostly to team leads. Aside from debugging really deep client cases (L3), generally, one doesn't need to see profile data at all

One more update here for <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U>
We completely drop the profile related tables from postgres. And I guess everyone have access to aerospike. let me know you if need something extra here.
<@U08C43RCH39> I don't have access to aerospike, could you please help with it?
<@U09CTDGV18D> You should ask access from your team lead. We shared access to the corresponded team-leaders
